metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rename the AC1 target from 'reduce path' to the actual shared confirmation seam (the emit/emit_text/leaf_confirm helpers in src/rebar/_commands/_confirm.py), and specify that the structural test spies THOSE helpers to prove create/link/transition route through them (no per-verb inline printing) — the confirmation line is built from the seam outcome, not a reduce/store-read.
evidence: Scope 1 quote: 'add call-count/monkeypatch assertions on the shared confirmation reduce path'
src/rebar/_commands/_confirm.py docstring: 'built ONLY from the CLI args plus the seam's outcome, never a follow-up store read'
src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:404-410 builds create's confirmation from the `res` dict via confirm_created('', res) — no reduce_ticket call
In this repo 'reduce' denotes reduce_ticket event replay (rebar.reducer, 100+ search hits); no such call exists in the confirm path
The plan's own alternative 'seam-spy' phrasing DOES map to a real construct (_confirm.emit/emit_text), so only the 'reduce path' label is refuted
findings.finding: The plan asserts a 'shared confirmation reduce path' whose confirmation lines are built via a reduce/store-read, but reading the merged code refutes any reduce in that flow: _confirm.py's docstring states the line is built 'ONLY from the CLI args plus the seam's outcome, never a follow-up store read', and composer.py:404-410 builds create's line from the returned `res` dict with no reduce_ticket call. The actual shared seam is the emit/emit_text helpers in _confirm.py, not a reduce path.
findings.location: Scope item 1 ('add call-count/monkeypatch assertions on the shared confirmation reduce path') and AC line 1 ('Reduce-path structural assertion exists (call-count or seam-spy)')
scenarios: Implementer reads AC1, searches for a reduce_ticket call in the confirmation flow to attach a call-count assertion to, finds none, and either stalls or writes an assertion against the wrong seam
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'shared confirmation reduce path' with 'shared confirmation emit seam (rebar._commands._confirm.emit / emit_text / leaf_confirm)' and state the assertion spies those helpers (monkeypatch/call-count) for create/link/transition, confirming each verb prints via the shared helper rather than a bespoke print, and that no follow-up reduce_ticket/store read is invoked to build the line.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

'in docs or the test suite as golden data'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the AC3 golden mapping is seeded from the parent's reviewed old→new table (the authoritative spec), not by snapshotting current code output, so it functions as an oracle rather than a change-detector.
evidence: Plan: 'record the per-verb old→new confirmation-line mapping (the parent's comment has the full table) in docs or the test suite as golden data.'
The parent's close-out comment 'has the full table' — indicating an authoritative source exists, so the golden data should be seeded from that reviewed mapping, not from live code output.
findings.finding: AC3's 'record the per-verb old->new confirmation-line mapping ... as golden data' risks the change-detector / self-authored-oracle anti-pattern if the golden values are captured by snapshotting whatever the code currently emits rather than asserting the intended/spec'd lines.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the AC2 classification test derives the covered-verb set from the existing `_CONFIRM_SCOPE` (`_WRITES_FULL` | `_LIFECYCLE`) registry and diffs it against the inventory (reusing the `test_readme_table_matches_registry` pattern), rather than hand-maintaining a parallel verb list.
evidence: The verb set is already enumerated authoritatively: src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:173 `_WRITES_FULL = frozenset({...})` and :476 `_CONFIRM_SCOPE = _WRITES_FULL | _LIFECYCLE`.

An existing registry-derived guard pattern exists: tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py:166 `test_readme_table_matches_registry` — the 'added-without-classification' check should reuse this style.
The parent already carries the full no-op-capable vs always-writes classification in its 2026-08-15 close-out comment, so the classification data need not be re-derived by hand.
findings.finding: AC2's verb-inventory classification test risks maintaining a parallel verb list that duplicates the existing authoritative registry (`_WRITES_FULL` + `_LIFECYCLE` = `_CONFIRM_SCOPE`), creating a second source of truth that can drift; the plan leaves the mechanism open ('generated or hand-maintained', 'docs/cli-reference or a test-enforced table') without pointing at the existing derivation seam.
findings.location: Scope item 2 / AC line 'Verb inventory (no-op-capable vs always-writes) lives in a durable, reviewable location and a test fails when a verb is added without classification.'
scenarios: A future verb is added to `_WRITES_FULL`/`_LIFECYCLE` but the hand-maintained inventory list is not updated, so the 'added-without-classification' test passes falsely because it checks a stale second list rather than diffing against `_CONFIRM_SCOPE`.
findings.suggested_fix: In scope item 2 / AC2, specify the enforcement seam: the test iterates `rebar._cli._CONFIRM_SCOPE` and asserts every member appears exactly once in the inventory table with a no-op-capable/always-writes classification, failing on any unclassified or stale entry — mirroring tests/unit/test_generated_surface_markers.py::test_readme_table_matches_registry.

If the author takes the cli-reference branch, a hand-added inventory table would be flagged stale/reverted by the drift gate unless scripts/gen_cli_reference.py is extended to emit it — an unenumerated edit target for that branch.

scenarios: Author hand-edits docs/cli-reference.md to add the inventory table; make lint / the CLI-reference drift gate then fails because the committed file no longer matches generator output.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve AC2's mode disjunction so the chosen location is one a test can enforce, and name the derivation: the enforcement test should read the verb set from _CONFIRM_SCOPE (_WRITES_FULL | _LIFECYCLE) and fail if any verb lacks a no-op-capable/always-writes classification.
evidence: Scope 2 offers a disjunction: 'as generated or hand-maintained documentation (docs/cli-reference or a test-enforced table)'
AC2 simultaneously requires 'a test fails when a verb is added without classification' — a hand-maintained docs table with no enforcing test does NOT meet this

A durable enumerable source of truth already exists in-repo: _CONFIRM_SCOPE = _WRITES_FULL | _LIFECYCLE (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:476) plus the no-op branches in leaf_confirm/_confirm_tag_outcome (_confirm.py) — the enforcement test can derive the verb set from _CONFIRM_SCOPE and assert every verb is classified, but the plan names neither the source set nor the derivation
findings.finding: AC2 permits a solution mode (hand-maintained/docs-only table) that cannot satisfy the same AC's enforcement clause, and does not name the load-bearing enforcement mechanism.
findings.location: Scope item 2 / AC line 2 ('Verb inventory ... lives in a durable, reviewable location and a test fails when a verb is added without classification')
scenarios: Implementer picks the docs-only branch, writes a prose table in cli-reference.md, and no test guards it — the AC's enforcement clause is silently unmet, exactly the residual the parent could not tick
A future verb added to _WRITES_FULL ships unclassified because the 'table' is prose the CI never checks
findings.suggested_fix: Specify a single mechanism: a test-enforced classification table (a Python mapping or a data file) whose keys are cross-checked against _CONFIRM_SCOPE, failing when a verb is present in the scope set but absent from the table (or vice versa). If a cli-reference table is also wanted, generate it from that same source via the existing gen_cli_reference drift-gate rather than hand-maintaining it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Disambiguate AC1: state which regression the structural assertion guards (per-verb re-printing that bypasses the shared _confirm seam, vs. a follow-up store read building the line) and pick the mechanism that actually catches THAT regression — or require both if both residuals are in scope.
evidence: Scope 1 names the goal as catching 'a future regression that bypasses the shared seam (printing per-verb again) ... structurally'
The parent AC1 residual actually named a DIFFERENT guarantee: 'no additional store read/reduce builds it (call-count or monkeypatch assertion on the reduce path)' (parent AC1)

These are distinct mechanisms against distinct regressions: a call-count spy on the store-read/reduce path proves the line is built from the seam outcome (no follow-up read), whereas a spy on the shared _confirm.emit/emit_text seam proves verbs route through the shared channel rather than print(...) themselves — neither one catches the other's regression
findings.finding: AC1 conflates two structurally different guarantees ('call-count' on the reduce path vs. 'seam-spy' for per-verb re-printing) under one 'call-count or seam-spy' choice, leaving the regression the assertion must catch ambiguous.
findings.location: Scope item 1 / AC line 1 ('Reduce-path structural assertion exists (call-count or seam-spy) covering at least create/link/transition')
scenarios: Implementer adds a monkeypatch call-count on the reduce path (satisfying the parent's literal wording) but a verb that regresses to a bespoke print() bypassing _confirm.emit is NOT caught, defeating the stated goal of Scope 1
Implementer spies only on _confirm.emit and a future verb reintroduces a follow-up store read to build its line — not caught
findings.suggested_fix: If the goal is 'no verb bypasses the shared seam', assert a spy on rebar._commands._confirm.emit/emit_text (and leaf_confirm) is the ONLY producer of the confirmation line for create/link/transition, with the store-read/reduce path call-count kept at zero to also cover the parent's 'no follow-up read' clause.
